ImageDescription.value: One of the many chapels named Our Lady of Salette, this one is atop Mont Pipet in Vienne. Photo taken from Saint-Just (another hill), with Mont Salomon in the background. Vienne, like Rome, is a city of many hills. ^_^ For a recently-uploaded close-up of Léonard Périer's statue in volcanic rock (pierre de Volvic), see here.

ImageDescription.value: On Saturdays, Vienne hosts the largest open-air market in Southeastern France.  As a result, on those days, if you're a wee one, you only see the second floor of the central building of the Place de Miremont.  You can see plenty of garlic and colorful paravents though. :)

ImageDescription.value: One of France's oldest churches, the Église Saint-Pierre in Vienne is home to a lapidarium. Taking advantage of a gate that is not usually open leading to the Institut Robin elementary school playground, I was able to take the southern façade, which has the advantage of not having a holy host of cars parked in front of it. :)
